allowedSourceMaterial.overview: An insurance investigator visits a small town while looking into the strange disappearance of a popular horror novelist. He soon finds that the impact of the author’s books is far more than inspirational.

facts.title: In the Mouth of Madness

visibleEditorialCopy.curiosityHook: What happens when the line between a bestselling horror writer's fiction and the physical world begins to blur?
visibleEditorialCopy.description: Looking into the strange disappearance of a famous horror novelist, an insurance investigator travels to an eerie small town where the frightening world of the author's books seems to be bleeding into reality.
visibleEditorialCopy.vibeSummary: Suspenseful, reality-warping horror with a steady, engaging pace best suited for focused late-night viewing alone.
visibleEditorialCopy.whyWatch: Directed by John Carpenter, this unsettling mystery blends psychological unease with supernatural dread as an ordinary inquiry unravels into reality-bending terror.

claudeAdvisory.claimSpan: the frightening world of the author's books seems to be bleeding into reality
issueSummaries: The overview says only that the investigator 'soon finds that the impact of the author's books is far more than inspirational', and it leaves the nature of that impact open. Every field of the copy resolves it into a specific mechanic: fiction bleeding into or blurring with reality. description says the author's world 'seems to be bleeding into reality', curiosityHook says 'the line between... fiction and the physical world begins to blur', vibeSummary says 'reality-warping', and whyWatch says 'reality-bending terror' and 'supernatural dread'. This is an unsupported causal and mechanistic concretization, and it sits close to the excluded 'later revelations' category, since it states what the discovery is.
curiosityHook calls the author 'bestselling'. The overview says 'popular', so this is a small unsupported factual attribute.
claudeAdvisory.sourceBoundaryReason: The core premise (insurance investigator, small town, the strange disappearance of a popular horror novelist, books with an effect beyond inspiration, the director, the genres) is grounded. The tonal language is tolerated genre shorthand under A_PRIME_PRODUCTION_MATERIALITY_V1. The recurring 'reality bleeding / blurring / bending' framing goes further. It takes the overview's open-ended teaser and states a specific supernatural mechanic in all four fields. That falsely specifies plot mechanics and what the central discovery is, and it edges toward the excluded 'later revelations' category. The copy hedges ('seems to be', 'begins to blur'), and it does not contradict the premise, invent identities, or reveal an outcome or ending, so the severity is MINOR and not SEVERE. A bounded fix would stay with the overview's own framing, for example 'an insurance investigator looks into a popular horror novelist's strange disappearance and soon finds that the author's books have an unsettling impact far beyond inspiration'.

sourceEvidence.notes: description, curiosityHook, vibeSummary, whyWatch: nothing in the overview says the books' content crosses into reality or that anything supernatural occurs. 'Far more than inspirational' is deliberately vague. The copy fills that gap with one specific interpretation, and it does so in all four fields.

description: the insurance investigator, the small town, and the strange disappearance of a horror novelist restate the overview. 'Famous' paraphrases 'popular'. 'Eerie' and 'frightening' are atmospheric flourishes for a horror-novelist premise and are tolerated.

whyWatch and vibeSummary: 'mystery', 'horror', 'unsettling', 'psychological unease' and 'supernatural dread' are consistent in general terms with genres Drama/Fantasy/Horror/Mystery/Thriller, and the Fantasy and Horror genres give some support to a supernatural register. 'John Carpenter' matches director. The genres support a horror and supernatural tone. They do not support the specific claim that fiction bleeds into reality.

acceptedSemanticClassification: 'Suspenseful', 'steady, engaging pace' and 'focused... viewing alone' match moods, pace=medium, attentionDemand=engaged and situations=[alone]. 'Late-night' is not an accepted situation, but it is a viewing-mood flourish. Keyword-only material (insanity, paranoia, Lovecraftian, ghost town, church) is not imported.

claudeAdvisory.uncertaintyNotes: This is a near-threshold call. The Fantasy and Horror genres make a supernatural reading plausible, and 'far more than inspirational' does imply something beyond ordinary influence, so an adjudicator could treat 'reality-bending' as tolerated genre shorthand and approve. I flag the fields because the same specific mechanic recurs in every field and answers the question the overview leaves open. Also, the hedged wording in description and curiosityHook is softer than the flat 'reality-bending terror' and 'reality-warping' in whyWatch and vibeSummary. If Sophia treats the hedged phrasings as acceptable, the concern would concentrate on those two fields. 'Bestselling' for 'popular' was considered and would be tolerated on its own.

geminiAdvisory.sourceBoundaryReason: All visible editorial copy strictly adheres to A_PRIME_PRODUCTION_MATERIALITY_V1. The narrative premise, small-town investigative framing, and reality-bending conflict in the description and curiosityHook faithfully track the authorized overview and keywords. The copy exercises disciplined setup-only restraint by omitting ungrounded character names (e.g., Sutter Cane, John Trent), specific scene-level mechanics, or third-act sanity/apocalyptic twists. Figurative phrasing such as 'bleeding into reality' and 'supernatural dread' functions as legitimate, low-risk atmospheric inference and genre shorthand capturing the authorized premise that the author's books exert an influence 'far more than inspirational'.

sourceEvidence.notes: Directly supports an insurance investigator traveling to a small town to look into the strange disappearance of a popular horror novelist, discovering that the impact of the author's books goes far beyond mere inspiration.
Directly verifies Horror, Mystery, Fantasy, and Thriller genres, supporting 'horror', 'mystery', and 'supernatural dread' descriptions across visible copy.

facts.director verifies John Carpenter. facts.keywords verifies 'author', 'disappearance', 'insurance investigator', 'lovecraftian', and 'small town'. Accepted semantic classification directly grounds pace: medium ('steady... pace'), attentionDemand: engaged ('engaging', 'focused'), moods: suspenseful ('Suspenseful', 'suspenseful'), and situations: alone ('viewing alone').
